# Requirements Specification: `axil_timer`

Task: prj-ada3a9b9d9:requirements
Serves project requirement: [requirement:req-2b2b91a584] "Create an AXI4-Lite timer peripheral with an interrupt."
Source: [document:prj-ada3a9b9d9.requirements.document.customer_requirements] (requirements.md, sha256:6db645a9167d681c12bc01d3de53afb4373151b05c31f50942aed7e315a6e019)
Standard followed: NIP-STD-003 Requirement Traceability
Status: DRAFT. This spec has not been reviewed; independent review is required before approval.

## 0. Conventions

- Every requirement keeps the customer's tag as its ID, unchanged. Later documents restate each requirement where it belongs, under the same tag.
- Every requirement holds as stated. The flow case judges each rule only within the scope listed by tag under `judged_scope` in `evals/flow/axil_timer/citations.json`. Rules that no check rests on are listed there under `not_judged`. That file is not part of this spec's inputs.
- Time words:
  - An *edge* is a rising edge of `aclk`.
  - A value "after edge E" is the value in the clock cycle that follows E.
  - A value "before edge E" is the value in the clock cycle that ends at E.
  - A transfer is accepted on an edge on which its VALID and READY are both high.
- Verification methods:
  - SIM: self-checking Icarus Verilog testbench, timed to the clock edge.
  - LINT: Verilator `--lint-only -Wall`.
  - SYN: Yosys synthesis.
  - INSP: inspection of the RTL or of the testbench.

## 1. The block

| ID | Requirement | Rationale | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| TMR-MODULE | One Verilog module named `axil_timer`. It is a 32-bit down-counting timer with a one-shot mode and a periodic mode and a level interrupt, behind an AXI4-Lite subordinate port. | Defines the deliverable the project requirement asks for. | INSP; SIM (instantiation) |
| TMR-ADDR-WIDTH | One parameter, `ADDR_WIDTH`, the byte address width. The block works at `ADDR_WIDTH` 4 and at 8. At 8, every offset from `0x10` up is unmapped. | The block must integrate into address spaces of different sizes. | SIM at width 4 and at width 8 |
| TMR-ADDR-WIDTH-RANGE | `ADDR_WIDTH` defaults to 4. The block also works at every width from 5 to 7, and there too every offset from `0x10` up is unmapped. | Makes the default explicit and covers the full supported range. | INSP (default value); SIM at a width above 4 |
| TMR-PORTS | All ports are synchronous to the rising edge of `aclk`. Ports: `aclk`; `aresetn` (active low); `s_axil_awaddr` (`ADDR_WIDTH` bits), `s_axil_awvalid`, `s_axil_awready`; `s_axil_wdata` (32 bits), `s_axil_wstrb` (4 bits, bit n enables bits 8n+7:8n), `s_axil_wvalid`, `s_axil_wready`; `s_axil_bresp` (2 bits), `s_axil_bvalid`, `s_axil_bready`; `s_axil_araddr` (`ADDR_WIDTH` bits), `s_axil_arvalid`, `s_axil_arready`; `s_axil_rdata` (32 bits), `s_axil_rresp` (2 bits), `s_axil_rvalid`, `s_axil_rready`; `irq` (1 bit, active high). Response `00` is OKAY and `10` is SLVERR. | A fixed interface allows integration and reuse of the testbench. | INSP; SIM (port connection) |
| TMR-PORTS-ONLY | The block has no ports other than those listed in TMR-PORTS. | Prevents hidden interfaces. | INSP; SIM (named connection compiles) |

## 2. Registers

| Offset | Name | Access | Reset value | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x0 | CTRL | read/write | 0x0 | bit 0 EN, bit 1 IE, bit 2 MODE; bits 31:3 read as zero |
| 0x4 | LOAD | read/write | 0x0 | count length, in clock cycles |
| 0x8 | COUNT | read only | 0x0 | cycles left in the current count |
| 0xC | STATUS | write 1 to clear | 0x0 | bit 0 EXPIRED; bits 31:1 read as zero |

| ID | Requirement | Rationale | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| TMR-MAP | The four registers sit at the offsets above, with the access types and reset values above. | The register map is the software contract. | SIM (reads after reset; write and read back) |
| TMR-CTRL-STRB | `CTRL` is written only when `wstrb[0]` is set. A `CTRL` write without `wstrb[0]` changes nothing and still answers OKAY. `IE` is the interrupt enable. `MODE` is 0 for one-shot and 1 for periodic. | Defines byte-enable semantics for a register whose fields all sit in byte 0. | SIM |
| TMR-LOAD | `LOAD` is written byte by byte as `wstrb` enables, and reads back what was written. | Supports partial-width writes. | SIM (per-byte strobes, read back) |
| TMR-STATUS-CLEAR | A write of 1 to bit 0 with `wstrb[0]` set clears `EXPIRED`. A write of 0, or a write without `wstrb[0]`, leaves `EXPIRED` as it is. | Write-1-to-clear avoids read-modify-write races. | SIM |

## 3. The timer

| ID | Requirement | Rationale | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| TMR-START | Writing `EN` 1 starts a count. On the edge the write takes effect (see TMR-COUNT-LENGTH), `COUNT` takes the value of `LOAD`. Writing `EN` 1 while a count runs restarts the count from `LOAD` in the same way. | Defines the start and restart semantics. | SIM |
| TMR-LOAD-ZERO | A `LOAD` of 0 counts as 1. A one-shot count started on edge E with `LOAD` 0 ends on edge E+1. | Removes the degenerate zero-length case. | SIM |
| TMR-LOAD-ZERO-PERIODIC | In periodic mode a `LOAD` of 0 also counts as 1. A count started on edge E with `LOAD` 0 ends on every edge E+1, E+2, and so on. | Same as above, for periodic mode. | SIM |
| TMR-COUNT | While `EN` is 1, `COUNT` goes down by one on every edge (the customer text adds: "what that needs of bits 31:21 is TMR-COUNT-32BIT, and what other transfers leave of it is TMR-RUNNING-UNDISTURBED"). There are two exceptions. (a) The edge that ends the count, which is an edge with `EN` 1 and `COUNT` 1 or 0 before it, sets `EXPIRED`. (b) On the restart edge, an edge on which a `CTRL` write with `EN` 1 takes effect, `COUNT` takes the value of `LOAD` instead. | This is the core counting behaviour. | SIM (cycle-exact) |
| TMR-COUNT-32BIT | `COUNT` is a full 32-bit value in every step. The decrement borrows through every bit up to bit 31. An edge ends the count only when all 32 bits of `COUNT` are 1 or 0 before it; a set high bit means the count is still running. The reload of a periodic count takes all 32 bits of `LOAD`. | Guards against truncated counters and truncated compares. | SIM (values with high bits set, borrow across bytes) |
| TMR-RUNNING-UNDISTURBED | A transfer that is not a `CTRL` write, a `LOAD` write or a `STATUS` clear leaves a running count as it is. This covers a read of any register, a write to `COUNT`, a write to an unmapped address, and a `STATUS` write that clears nothing. None of these changes `COUNT` or stalls, restarts or stops its decrement, so the count ends on the same edge as it would without the transfer. | Bus activity must not perturb timing. | SIM |
| TMR-COUNT-LENGTH | A write takes effect on the edge that completes it (section 4), which is the edge after which `s_axil_bvalid` is first high for that write. A count started on edge E with `LOAD` N (N at least 1) ends on edge E+N. In periodic mode it ends again on E+2N, E+3N, and so on. When `IE` is 1, `irq` is high after the edge that ends the count. | Exact, testable timing. | SIM (cycle-exact) |
| TMR-COUNT-READ | After the start edge E of a count with `LOAD` N (N at least 1), `COUNT` is N−k after edge E+k, for k from 0 to N−1. With `LOAD` 0, `COUNT` takes 0 on the start edge, not 1, and stays 0. | Makes the observable value of `COUNT` exact. | SIM |
| TMR-ONESHOT | In one-shot mode (`MODE` 0), the edge that ends the count sets `COUNT` to 0 and clears `EN` itself. `CTRL` then reads `EN` 0, and nothing more happens and no second interrupt comes until `EN` is written 1 again. | One-shot semantics. | SIM |
| TMR-PERIODIC | In periodic mode (`MODE` 1), the edge that ends the count loads `COUNT` from `LOAD` again and `EN` stays 1. With `LOAD` at least 1, every period is exactly `LOAD` cycles. For a `LOAD` of 0, see TMR-LOAD-ZERO-PERIODIC. | Periodic semantics with no drift. | SIM (several periods) |
| TMR-PERIODIC-EXPIRED-SET | A periodic count ends and reloads at the end of every period whether or not `EXPIRED` is already set. Nothing has to clear `EXPIRED` between two periods. | Periodic operation must not depend on software servicing. | SIM |
| TMR-RESTART-MODE | A `CTRL` write that writes `EN` 1 while a count runs (a restart) sets `MODE` as well. The restarted count ends as the new `MODE` says, one-shot or periodic, not as the `MODE` it was started with. | Removes ambiguity on restart. | SIM |
| TMR-LOAD-END-EDGE | Suppose a `LOAD` write takes effect on the edge a periodic count ends. This document states no rule for what that edge reloads: the value `LOAD` held before the edge, or the value the write gives it. A test accepts both. | This is the only choice the customer leaves open. | SIM (accepts both outcomes) |
| TMR-STOP | Writing `EN` 0 stops the count. After the edge the write takes effect, `EN` reads 0 and `COUNT` keeps the value that edge gave it. No more counts end until `EN` is written 1 again. | Stop semantics. | SIM |
| TMR-STOP-EDGE | The stop edge is still an edge of the running count. Unless it ends the count, `COUNT` goes down by one on it, so after the stop `COUNT` is one less than before the stop edge. Writing `EN` 0 while `EN` is already 0 leaves `COUNT` as it is. | Exact value of `COUNT` at a stop. | SIM |
| TMR-CTRL-WINS | A `CTRL` write that takes effect on the edge a count ends wins for `EN` and `COUNT`. With `EN` 1: `EN` stays 1 and `COUNT` takes the value of `LOAD`, so the count restarts. With `EN` 0: `EN` is 0 after that edge, and `COUNT` takes what the count end gives it under the `MODE` held before that edge, not the `MODE` the write sets. That value is 0 when that `MODE` is 0 (one-shot) and the value of `LOAD` when it is 1 (periodic); `COUNT` then keeps that value. In both cases `EXPIRED` is still set by the count that ended. | Resolves a same-edge collision exactly. | SIM |
| TMR-END-BEATS-CLEAR | A count end beats a clear. When a `STATUS` clear takes effect on the edge a count ends, in one-shot or periodic mode, `EXPIRED` stays set. | No interrupt event is lost. | SIM |
| TMR-IRQ | `irq` is `EXPIRED` AND `IE`, as a level: high when both are 1 and low otherwise. It stays high until `EXPIRED` is cleared or `IE` is written 0. Writing `IE` 1 while `EXPIRED` is set raises it. | Level interrupt semantics. | SIM |
| TMR-IRQ-EDGE | `irq` has no delay of its own. It changes after the very edge on which a write that sets or clears `IE`, or a `STATUS` clear, takes effect. | Exact interrupt timing. | SIM |

## 4. Transfers

| ID | Requirement | Rationale | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| TMR-ORDER | Write address and write data may arrive in either order or together. A write completes on the edge that accepts the second of them, or both together. | AXI4-Lite channel independence. | SIM (all three orders) |
| TMR-READY | One outstanding transaction per direction. `s_axil_awready` is high if and only if no write address is held and `s_axil_bvalid` is low. `s_axil_wready` is high if and only if no write data is held and `s_axil_bvalid` is low. `s_axil_arready` is high if and only if `s_axil_rvalid` is low. A write address is held after the edge that accepts it without its write data, until the edge that accepts that data. Write data is held after the edge that accepts it without its address, until the edge that accepts that address. After the edge that completes a write, nothing is held. | Exact handshake behaviour. | SIM |
| TMR-READY-HELD-REQUEST | A transfer is accepted only on an edge on which its VALID and READY are both high. So no new write address or data is accepted while a write response waits, and no new read address while a read response waits, even when one is offered. | Prevents lost or duplicated transfers. | SIM (back-pressure) |
| TMR-RESPONSE | Write response: `s_axil_bvalid` never rises before the write completes. Once high, it stays high with `s_axil_bresp` stable until an edge on which `s_axil_bready` is high, and is low after that edge. Read response: `s_axil_rvalid` never rises before the read address is accepted. Once high, it stays high with `s_axil_rresp` stable (and `s_axil_rdata` stable too when the read is of `COUNT`) until an edge on which `s_axil_rready` is high, and is low after that edge. | AXI response stability. | SIM (stalled READY) |
| TMR-RESPONSE-RDATA-STABLE | For a read of `CTRL`, `LOAD`, `STATUS` or an unmapped address, `s_axil_rdata` stays what it was when `s_axil_rvalid` rose for as long as `s_axil_rvalid` waits. This holds even if that register changes meanwhile, for example when a count end sets `EXPIRED` or a write changes `CTRL` or `LOAD`. | Read data must not tear. | SIM |
| TMR-RESPONSE-EDGE | `s_axil_bvalid` is high after the same edge that completes the write, not a later one. `s_axil_rvalid` is high after the same edge that accepts the read address, not a later one. Both hold while the response's READY is low on that edge. | Exact response latency. | SIM |
| TMR-RESPONSE-EDGE-READY-HIGH | When `s_axil_bready` is already high on the edge that completes a write, `s_axil_bvalid` is still high after that edge, for the one cycle it takes to be taken. Likewise, `s_axil_rvalid` is high after the edge that accepts a read address with `s_axil_rready` already high. A response is not skipped because its READY is early. | Every transfer gets exactly one response. | SIM |
| TMR-READ-VALUE | A read returns the value the register holds before the edge that accepts its address, not the value that edge gives it. | Exact read sampling point. | SIM |

## 5. Responses and unmapped addresses

| ID | Requirement | Rationale | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| TMR-DECODE | An address is mapped only when it is word aligned (`addr[1:0]` is 0) and below `0x10`. Every other address is unmapped and never aliases a register. | Full decode with no aliasing. | SIM (misaligned addresses; offsets ≥ 0x10 at width > 4) |
| TMR-SLVERR | An unmapped write, and any write to `COUNT`, changes nothing and gets SLVERR. An unmapped read returns zero with SLVERR. Every other transfer gets OKAY. | Error reporting to software. | SIM |

## 6. Reset

| ID | Requirement | Rationale | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| TMR-RESET | `aresetn` is active low. Reset puts every register at its reset value, stops the count and clears `EXPIRED`. `irq` is low after reset. | Known initial state. | SIM |
| TMR-RESET-EDGE | `aresetn` is synchronous: it is sampled on the rising edge of `aclk`, and every edge on which it is low resets the block. After such an edge, `s_axil_bvalid` and `s_axil_rvalid` are low and no write address or write data is held, whatever was in progress. The manager does not start a transfer while `aresetn` is low. | Exact reset timing, including reset in the middle of a transfer. | SIM (reset during a transaction and during a count) |

## 7. Implementation and verification

| ID | Requirement | Rationale | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| TMR-CLEAN | The RTL is clean under Verilator `--lint-only -Wall` with no waivers, and Yosys synthesis infers no latches. | Code quality and synthesizability. | LINT; SYN |
| TMR-TB | A self-checking testbench passes under Icarus Verilog on a block that meets this document. It instantiates the block at `ADDR_WIDTH` 4 and at a width above 4. | Provides executable evidence. | SIM; INSP |
| TMR-TB-ALL | The testbench checks every requirement in sections 2 to 6, with each count timed to the clock edge. | Complete coverage of the behavioural requirements. | INSP (trace from each tag to its checks); SIM |
| TMR-TEST-RANGE | Tests accept the whole allowed range. A testbench checks only what this document states, accepts every behaviour it allows, and never requires one choice where this document leaves a choice open. The only timing or response choice left open is the one TMR-LOAD-END-EDGE names; every other rule in sections 3 to 6 is exact. | Avoids over-constrained tests. | INSP |

## 8. Traceability

- Every ID above traces to [requirement:req-2b2b91a584] through the customer document named in the header.
- The tags are kept unchanged so that later documents (design, RTL, testbench) can restate each one under the same ID.

## 9. Assumptions and open points for the reviewer

1. TMR-COUNT refers to "bits 31:21". This may be a typo; the intended range may be 31:1 or the full 32 bits. The customer text is kept as written. TMR-COUNT-32BIT states the full 32-bit requirement unambiguously, and this spec relies on it.
2. The judged scope per tag lives in `evals/flow/axil_timer/citations.json`, which is not an input to this task. This spec does not restate that file's contents.
3. When `COUNT` is read while its value changes, TMR-RESPONSE requires `s_axil_rdata` to be stable, and TMR-READ-VALUE defines which value is returned. Together these imply the read data is captured on the edge that accepts the address.
4. There is no conflict between TMR-STOP-EDGE and TMR-CTRL-WINS. If the stop edge ends the count, TMR-CTRL-WINS governs the value of `COUNT`.
5. This spec has not been reviewed. Approval requires an independent review record.

# Interface Specification: `axil_timer`

Task: prj-ada3a9b9d9:interface-spec
Serves: [requirement:req-2b2b91a584] "Create an AXI4-Lite timer peripheral with an interrupt."
Derived from: [artifact:prj-ada3a9b9d9.requirements.a2] (axil_timer_requirements_spec.md, sha256:8ff3c71f0262b07ed726a784e2bf23c712e075d98ecc874209a8d2b4e1e199a8)
Status: DRAFT. Not reviewed. Approval requires an independent review record.

Every rule below keeps the requirement tag it restates. If this document and the requirements spec ever differ, the requirements spec governs, and the difference must be escalated.

## 0. Conventions

- An *edge* is a rising edge of `aclk`.
- A value "after edge E" is the value in the clock cycle that follows E. A value "before edge E" is the value in the clock cycle that ends at E.
- A transfer on a channel is *accepted* on an edge on which that channel's VALID and READY are both high (TMR-READY-HELD-REQUEST).
- A write *completes* on the edge that accepts the second of its address and data, or on the edge that accepts both together (TMR-ORDER).
- A write *takes effect* on the edge that completes it (TMR-COUNT-LENGTH).
- Response codes: `2'b00` = OKAY, `2'b10` = SLVERR (TMR-PORTS). No other code is ever driven.

## 1. Parameter

| Name | Default | Legal range | Meaning | Tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ADDR_WIDTH` | 4 | 4 to 8 inclusive | Byte address width of `s_axil_awaddr` and `s_axil_araddr`. At widths above 4, every offset from `0x10` up is unmapped. | TMR-ADDR-WIDTH, TMR-ADDR-WIDTH-RANGE |

The block has exactly one parameter.

## 2. Ports (TMR-PORTS, TMR-PORTS-ONLY)

All ports are synchronous to the rising edge of `aclk`. The block has no other ports.

| Port | Dir | Width | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aclk` | in | 1 | Clock. |
| `aresetn` | in | 1 | Synchronous reset, active low (section 7). |
| `s_axil_awaddr` | in | `ADDR_WIDTH` | Write address (byte). |
| `s_axil_awvalid` | in | 1 | Write address valid. |
| `s_axil_awready` | out | 1 | Write address ready. |
| `s_axil_wdata` | in | 32 | Write data. |
| `s_axil_wstrb` | in | 4 | Byte strobes. Bit n enables `wdata[8n+7:8n]`. |
| `s_axil_wvalid` | in | 1 | Write data valid. |
| `s_axil_wready` | out | 1 | Write data ready. |
| `s_axil_bresp` | out | 2 | Write response (OKAY / SLVERR). |
| `s_axil_bvalid` | out | 1 | Write response valid. |
| `s_axil_bready` | in | 1 | Write response ready. |
| `s_axil_araddr` | in | `ADDR_WIDTH` | Read address (byte). |
| `s_axil_arvalid` | in | 1 | Read address valid. |
| `s_axil_arready` | out | 1 | Read address ready. |
| `s_axil_rdata` | out | 32 | Read data. |
| `s_axil_rresp` | out | 2 | Read response (OKAY / SLVERR). |
| `s_axil_rvalid` | out | 1 | Read data valid. |
| `s_axil_rready` | in | 1 | Read data ready. |
| `irq` | out | 1 | Level interrupt, active high (section 6). |

AXI4-Lite has no `AWPROT`/`ARPROT` ports on this block. TMR-PORTS-ONLY excludes them.

## 3. Channels: handshake, ordering and timing

### 3.1 Outstanding transactions (TMR-READY)

At most one write and at most one read may be outstanding at a time. The write path and the read path are independent of each other.

### 3.2 Write address channel (AW)

- `s_axil_awready` is high **if and only if** no write address is held **and** `s_axil_bvalid` is low (TMR-READY).
- A write address is *held* after the edge that accepts it without its write data. It stays held until the edge that accepts that data (TMR-READY).
- No AW transfer is accepted while a write response waits, even when `s_axil_awvalid` is high (TMR-READY-HELD-REQUEST).

### 3.3 Write data channel (W)

- `s_axil_wready` is high **if and only if** no write data is held **and** `s_axil_bvalid` is low (TMR-READY).
- Write data is *held* after the edge that accepts it without its address. It stays held until the edge that accepts that address (TMR-READY).
- No W transfer is accepted while a write response waits (TMR-READY-HELD-REQUEST).

### 3.4 AW/W ordering (TMR-ORDER)

There are three legal orders, and all are supported:

1. AW accepted before W: the write completes on the edge that accepts W.
2. W accepted before AW: the write completes on the edge that accepts AW.
3. AW and W accepted on the same edge: the write completes on that edge.

After the completing edge, nothing is held (TMR-READY).

### 3.5 Write response channel (B)

- `s_axil_bvalid` never rises before the write completes (TMR-RESPONSE).
- `s_axil_bvalid` is high after the same edge that completes the write, not a later one. This holds whatever `s_axil_bready` is on that edge (TMR-RESPONSE-EDGE, TMR-RESPONSE-EDGE-READY-HIGH).
  - If `s_axil_bready` is already high on the completing edge, `s_axil_bvalid` is still high for one cycle after it. A response is never skipped.
- Once high, `s_axil_bvalid` stays high with `s_axil_bresp` stable until an edge on which `s_axil_bready` is high. It is low after that edge (TMR-RESPONSE).
- While `s_axil_bvalid` is high, `s_axil_awready` and `s_axil_wready` are low (TMR-READY).

### 3.6 Read address channel (AR)

- `s_axil_arready` is high **if and only if** `s_axil_rvalid` is low (TMR-READY).
- No AR transfer is accepted while a read response waits (TMR-READY-HELD-REQUEST).

### 3.7 Read data channel (R)

- `s_axil_rvalid` never rises before the read address is accepted (TMR-RESPONSE).
- `s_axil_rvalid` is high after the same edge that accepts the read address. This holds even when `s_axil_rready` is already high on that edge (TMR-RESPONSE-EDGE, TMR-RESPONSE-EDGE-READY-HIGH).
- Once high, `s_axil_rvalid` stays high until an edge on which `s_axil_rready` is high. It is low after that edge (TMR-RESPONSE).
- While `s_axil_rvalid` is high, `s_axil_rresp` and `s_axil_rdata` are stable for every address, including `COUNT`, unmapped addresses, and registers that change meanwhile (TMR-RESPONSE, TMR-RESPONSE-RDATA-STABLE).
- **Read sampling point:** a read returns the value the register held *before* the edge that accepts its address (TMR-READ-VALUE). The read data is therefore captured on the accepting edge.

### 3.8 Interaction between reads and writes

- Reads and writes proceed independently.
- A read accepted on the same edge on which a write takes effect returns the value held before that edge (TMR-READ-VALUE).
- No transfer other than a `CTRL` write, a `LOAD` write or a `STATUS` clear changes a running count (TMR-RUNNING-UNDISTURBED). This includes:
  - any read;
  - a write to `COUNT`;
  - an unmapped write;
  - a `STATUS` write that clears nothing.

## 4. Address decode and error responses

### 4.1 Decode (TMR-DECODE)

An address is mapped only when **both** of these hold:

- `addr[1:0] == 2'b00`, and
- the address is below `0x10`.

Every other address is unmapped, never aliases a register, and is treated as in 4.2. At `ADDR_WIDTH` 4, the unmapped addresses are the misaligned ones. At widths 5 to 8, the unmapped addresses are also every offset ≥ `0x10`.

### 4.2 Responses (TMR-SLVERR, TMR-CTRL-STRB)

| Transfer | Effect | Response | rdata |
|---|---|---|---|
| Write to unmapped address (any `wstrb`) | none | SLVERR | — |
| Write to `COUNT` (0x8), any `wstrb` | none | SLVERR | — |
| Write to `CTRL`, `LOAD`, `STATUS` (any `wstrb`, including `4'b0000`) | per section 5 | OKAY | — |
| Read of unmapped address | none | SLVERR | `32'h0` |
| Read of `CTRL`, `LOAD`, `COUNT`, `STATUS` | none | OKAY | register value (3.7) |

## 5. Register map (TMR-MAP)

The same map is given as data in `register_map.json`. Unlisted bits read as zero and ignore writes.

| Offset | Name | Access | Reset | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x0 | CTRL | rw | 0x0 | [0] EN, [1] IE, [2] MODE (0 one-shot, 1 periodic); [31:3] read 0 |
| 0x4 | LOAD | rw | 0x0 | [31:0] VALUE: count length in clock cycles |
| 0x8 | COUNT | ro | 0x0 | [31:0] VALUE: cycles left in the current count |
| 0xC | STATUS | w1c | 0x0 | [0] EXPIRED (w1c); [31:1] read 0 |

### 5.1 Byte-strobe semantics

- **CTRL** (TMR-CTRL-STRB): written only when `wstrb[0]` is 1. In that case EN, IE and MODE all take `wdata[2:0]`. Without `wstrb[0]`, nothing changes and the response is OKAY.
- **LOAD** (TMR-LOAD): each byte n is written when `wstrb[n]` is 1. A read returns what was written.
- **STATUS** (TMR-STATUS-CLEAR): EXPIRED is cleared only by a write with `wstrb[0]` = 1 and `wdata[0]` = 1. A write of 0, or a write without `wstrb[0]`, leaves EXPIRED unchanged.
- **COUNT**: not writable. A write gets SLVERR (4.2).

### 5.2 Hardware-side register behaviour

Hardware also changes the registers, as follows:

- **EN**: cleared by hardware at the end of a one-shot count (TMR-ONESHOT).
- **COUNT**: changed only by the timer (TMR-COUNT, TMR-COUNT-32BIT).
- **EXPIRED**: set by hardware at every count end. A count end beats a same-edge clear (TMR-END-BEATS-CLEAR).

The full timer behaviour is defined by these requirement tags, which the design spec restates:

TMR-START, TMR-LOAD-ZERO, TMR-LOAD-ZERO-PERIODIC, TMR-COUNT, TMR-COUNT-32BIT, TMR-RUNNING-UNDISTURBED, TMR-COUNT-LENGTH, TMR-COUNT-READ, TMR-ONESHOT, TMR-PERIODIC, TMR-PERIODIC-EXPIRED-SET, TMR-RESTART-MODE, TMR-LOAD-END-EDGE, TMR-STOP, TMR-STOP-EDGE, TMR-CTRL-WINS.

The key interface timing is:

- A count started on edge E (the completing edge of the `CTRL` write with EN = 1) with LOAD = N ≥ 1 ends on edge E+N.
- A count with LOAD = 0 ends on edge E+1.

## 6. Interrupt (TMR-IRQ, TMR-IRQ-EDGE)

- `irq = EXPIRED & IE`. It is a level signal with no added delay.
- `irq` changes after the very edge on which any of these happens:
  - a count end sets EXPIRED;
  - a `CTRL` write sets or clears IE;
  - a `STATUS` clear takes effect.
- Writing IE = 1 while EXPIRED is set raises `irq`.
- `irq` is low after reset.

## 7. Reset (TMR-RESET, TMR-RESET-EDGE)

`aresetn` is active low and synchronous. Every edge on which `aresetn` is low resets the block. After such an edge:

- every register is at its reset value, the count is stopped, EXPIRED is 0 and `irq` is 0;
- `s_axil_bvalid` = 0 and `s_axil_rvalid` = 0;
- no write address or write data is held, whatever was in progress.

The manager does not start a transfer while `aresetn` is low.

## 8. Open points for the reviewer

1. TMR-COUNT quotes "bits 31:21". This spec relies on TMR-COUNT-32BIT: `COUNT` and its decrement, end compare and reload are all 32 bits.
2. TMR-LOAD-END-EDGE is the only choice left open: whether a `LOAD` write that takes effect on a periodic count-end edge reloads the old or the new `LOAD` value. Both outcomes are allowed (TMR-TEST-RANGE).
3. The upstream requirements spec is itself unreviewed. Its approval was recorded by the evaluation rule, not by a judgement.
4. The key names in `register_map.json` follow the documented field list. Conformance to `nirmaan.models.RegisterMap` has not yet been checked.

# Microarchitecture Specification: `axil_timer`

Task: prj-ada3a9b9d9:microarchitecture
Serves: [requirement:req-2b2b91a584] "Create an AXI4-Lite timer peripheral with an interrupt."
Derived from:
- [artifact:prj-ada3a9b9d9.interface-spec.a2] (axil_timer_interface_spec.md, sha256:6a1f948a9566c9307e65e587cb80af71064f9213645337854a98393b795fd44d)
- [artifact:prj-ada3a9b9d9.interface-spec.a3] (register_map.json, sha256:4e3581d5ebd44f1094a430d75ce6385b5d3a9bcbb8187f398e53a511a2455e0a)

Status: DRAFT. Not reviewed. Upstream approvals were recorded by evaluation rule, not by judgement ([evidence:prj-ada3a9b9d9.interface-spec.e2]). Section numbers "IF x.y" refer to the interface spec. If this document and the interface spec differ, the interface spec governs and the difference must be escalated.

## 1. Conventions

- An *edge* is a rising edge of `aclk`. All state is in flops clocked by `aclk`.
- Signal names ending in `_q` are flops. Names without `_q` are combinational.
- `aresetn` is synchronous and has priority over every other next-state term (IF 7).

## 2. Block structure

```
          +-------------------- axil_timer ---------------------+
 AW ----->| wr_front (aw/w hold regs) --> wr_decode --+--> B    |
 W  ----->|                                           |         |
          |                                           v         |
          |                                   regfile (CTRL,    |
          |                                   LOAD, STATUS)     |
          |                                     |      ^        |
          |                                     v      |        |
          |                                   counter (COUNT)   |
 AR ----->| rd_decode/mux --(capture)--> r_reg ----------> R    |
          |                                   irq = EXPIRED&IE ->| irq
          +-----------------------------------------------------+
```

The design has a single clock domain and no CDC. It has no pipelines beyond the single response registers. There is no arbitration, because the write and read paths are independent (IF 3.1, IF 3.8) and only one write can take effect per edge.

## 3. State inventory

| Flop | Width | Reset | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aw_held_q` | 1 | 0 | A write address is held (IF 3.2) |
| `aw_addr_q` | ADDR_WIDTH | 0 | Held write address |
| `w_held_q` | 1 | 0 | Write data is held (IF 3.3) |
| `wdata_q` | 32 | 0 | Held write data |
| `wstrb_q` | 4 | 0 | Held write strobes |
| `bvalid_q` | 1 | 0 | Drives `s_axil_bvalid` |
| `bresp_q` | 2 | 0 | Drives `s_axil_bresp` |
| `rvalid_q` | 1 | 0 | Drives `s_axil_rvalid` |
| `rresp_q` | 2 | 0 | Drives `s_axil_rresp` |
| `rdata_q` | 32 | 0 | Drives `s_axil_rdata` |
| `en_q`, `ie_q`, `mode_q` | 1 each | 0 | CTRL[0], CTRL[1], CTRL[2] |
| `load_q` | 32 | 0 | LOAD |
| `count_q` | 32 | 0 | COUNT (TMR-COUNT-32BIT) |
| `expired_q` | 1 | 0 | STATUS[0] |

Total: 117 + 2×ADDR_WIDTH... more precisely 4 + ADDR_WIDTH + 32 + 4 + 3 + 3 + 32 + 3 + 32 + 32 + 1 = 146 + ADDR_WIDTH flops. There are no memories and no other state.

## 4. Buffers and depth justification

| Buffer | Depth | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| AW hold (`aw_held_q`, `aw_addr_q`) | 1 | At most one write is outstanding (IF 3.1). `awready` is low while an address is held (IF 3.2), so a second address can never arrive. |
| W hold (`w_held_q`, `wdata_q`, `wstrb_q`) | 1 | Same argument (IF 3.3). |
| B response (`bvalid_q`, `bresp_q`) | 1 | At most one write is outstanding. `awready` and `wready` are low while `bvalid_q` is high (IF 3.5), so no new write can complete while a response waits. |
| R response (`rvalid_q`, `rresp_q`, `rdata_q`) | 1 | At most one read is outstanding. `arready` is low while `rvalid_q` is high (IF 3.6). |

Invariant W-1: `aw_held_q & w_held_q` is never 1. The second of AW and W completes the write on its accepting edge (IF 3.4), so neither is held after that edge.

Invariant W-2: `bvalid_q` implies `~aw_held_q & ~w_held_q`. Nothing is accepted while `bvalid_q` is high. A hold is created only with `bvalid_q` low, and `bvalid_q` rises only on the completing edge, which clears both holds.

No buffer can grow without bound, and every buffer is bounded by a ready that is low while it is occupied.

## 5. Write path (cycle level)

### 5.1 Ready and handshake

```
awready = ~aw_held_q & ~bvalid_q            // IF 3.2
wready  = ~w_held_q  & ~bvalid_q            // IF 3.3
aw_hs   = s_axil_awvalid & awready
w_hs    = s_axil_wvalid  & wready
wr_complete = (aw_hs | aw_held_q) & (w_hs | w_held_q)   // IF 3.4, all three orders
```

Both ready outputs come directly from flops, with no combinational path from any input. By W-2, `wr_complete` implies that `bvalid_q` is 0.

### 5.2 Effective write operands (on the completing edge)

```
eff_addr = aw_held_q ? aw_addr_q : s_axil_awaddr
eff_data = w_held_q  ? wdata_q   : s_axil_wdata
eff_strb = w_held_q  ? wstrb_q   : s_axil_wstrb
```

### 5.3 Hold registers next state

```
aw_held_q <= ~wr_complete & (aw_held_q | aw_hs)
w_held_q  <= ~wr_complete & (w_held_q  | w_hs)
if (aw_hs) aw_addr_q <= s_axil_awaddr
if (w_hs)  {wdata_q, wstrb_q} <= {s_axil_wdata, s_axil_wstrb}
```

### 5.4 B channel

```
if (wr_complete)            {bvalid_q, bresp_q} <= {1, wr_err ? 2'b10 : 2'b00}
else if (s_axil_bready)     bvalid_q <= 0          // bresp_q holds
```

- `bvalid` is high after the completing edge, whatever `bready` was on that edge (TMR-RESPONSE-EDGE, TMR-RESPONSE-EDGE-READY-HIGH). The response cannot be skipped, because `bvalid_q` was 0 on that edge.
- `bresp_q` changes only on `wr_complete`, which cannot occur while `bvalid_q` is 1. It is therefore stable while valid (TMR-RESPONSE).

### 5.5 Throughput

The minimum spacing between write completions is 2 edges: the response must be accepted before `awready` and `wready` return. This is the maximum rate IF 3.5 allows. It is not a requirement to exceed it.

## 6. Decode and register access

### 6.1 Decode (TMR-DECODE)

```
mapped(a) = (a[1:0] == 2'b00) & (ADDR_WIDTH == 4 ? 1 : (a[ADDR_WIDTH-1:4] == 0))
idx(a)    = a[3:2]       // 0 CTRL, 1 LOAD, 2 COUNT, 3 STATUS
```

The RTL must generate the upper-bit test so that it elaborates cleanly when ADDR_WIDTH = 4 (no `[3:4]` slice).

### 6.2 Write decode (IF 4.2, IF 5.1)

```
wr_err      = ~mapped(eff_addr) | (idx(eff_addr) == 2)        // unmapped or COUNT
we_ctrl     = wr_complete & mapped & idx==0 & eff_strb[0]     // TMR-CTRL-STRB
we_load[n]  = wr_complete & mapped & idx==1 & eff_strb[n]     // TMR-LOAD, n = 0..3
clr_expired = wr_complete & mapped & idx==3 & eff_strb[0] & eff_data[0]   // TMR-STATUS-CLEAR
```

- A CTRL write with `wstrb[0]` = 0, and a STATUS write that clears nothing, return OKAY with no effect.
- A COUNT write or an unmapped write returns SLVERR with no effect (TMR-RUNNING-UNDISTURBED).

### 6.3 Read path (IF 3.6, IF 3.7)

```
arready = ~rvalid_q
ar_hs   = s_axil_arvalid & arready
if (ar_hs) {rvalid_q, rresp_q, rdata_q} <= {1, rd_err ? 2'b10 : 2'b00, rd_mux}
else if (s_axil_rready) rvalid_q <= 0
rd_err  = ~mapped(s_axil_araddr)
rd_mux  = rd_err ? 32'h0 :
          idx==0 ? {29'b0, mode_q, ie_q, en_q} :
          idx==1 ? load_q :
          idx==2 ? count_q :
                   {31'b0, expired_q}
```

- `rd_mux` reads the pre-edge flop values, and the capture happens on the accepting edge. A read therefore returns the value before that edge, even when a write takes effect on the same edge (TMR-READ-VALUE, IF 3.8).
- `rdata_q` and `rresp_q` change only on `ar_hs`, which cannot occur while `rvalid_q` is 1. They are therefore stable while valid, including for COUNT (TMR-RESPONSE-RDATA-STABLE).
- Reads have no side effects.

## 7. Timer counter (PROPOSAL: open points OP-1 to OP-6)

The only timing this section can ground in its inputs is IF 5.2:

- A count started on edge E with LOAD = N ≥ 1 ends on edge E+N.
- A count with LOAD = 0 ends on E+1.

Everything else in this section is a proposal pending the texts of TMR-START, TMR-STOP, TMR-STOP-EDGE, TMR-LOAD-ZERO, TMR-LOAD-ZERO-PERIODIC, TMR-PERIODIC, TMR-RESTART-MODE, TMR-CTRL-WINS and TMR-COUNT-READ.

```
start      = we_ctrl & eff_data[0] & ~en_q                   // OP-1: 0->1 only?
stop       = we_ctrl & ~eff_data[0]
running    = en_q
at_end     = ~|count_q[31:1]                                 // count_q is 0 or 1
count_end  = running & ~we_ctrl & at_end                     // OP-5: CTRL write wins

count_q <= start                 ? load_q :
           count_end &  mode_q   ? load_q :                  // OP-3, OP-4 reload
           count_end & ~mode_q   ? 32'h0  :
           running & ~we_ctrl    ? count_q - 1 :
           count_q                                           // OP-2: value on stop
en_q    <= we_ctrl ? eff_data[0] : (count_end & ~mode_q) ? 1'b0 : en_q    // TMR-ONESHOT
expired_q <= count_end ? 1'b1 : clr_expired ? 1'b0 : expired_q          // TMR-END-BEATS-CLEAR
ie_q, mode_q <= we_ctrl ? eff_data[2:1] : unchanged
load_q byte n <= we_load[n] ? eff_data[8n+7:8n] : unchanged
```

Check against IF 5.2:

- **LOAD = N ≥ 1.** After E, `count_q` = N. After E+k, `count_q` = N−k. Before E+N, `count_q` = 1, so `count_end` fires on E+N.
- **LOAD = 0.** After E, `count_q` = 0, so `count_end` fires on E+1.

The comparator is a 31-input NOR. The decrement is a 32-bit decrementer. These are the only wide combinational paths.

On a periodic count end, `load_q` is the pre-edge value. A LOAD write on the same edge therefore reloads the old value. IF 8 item 2 allows either choice (TMR-LOAD-END-EDGE).

## 8. Interrupt (TMR-IRQ, TMR-IRQ-EDGE)

```
irq = expired_q & ie_q
```

`irq` is driven from flops by one AND gate. It changes after the same edge as `expired_q` or `ie_q`.

## 9. Reset (TMR-RESET, TMR-RESET-EDGE)

On every edge with `aresetn` = 0, all flops in section 3 take their reset value. This stops the count, clears both holds and clears `bvalid_q` and `rvalid_q`. `irq` is then 0.

## 10. Backpressure, end to end

| Point | Stalled by | Effect upstream |
|---|---|---|
| AW | `aw_held_q` or `bvalid_q` | `awready` = 0; the manager holds AW |
| W | `w_held_q` or `bvalid_q` | `wready` = 0; the manager holds W |
| B | `bready` = 0 | `bvalid_q` holds, which blocks AW and W |
| AR | `rvalid_q` | `arready` = 0 |
| R | `rready` = 0 | `rvalid_q` holds, which blocks AR |
| Register file and counter | never | They accept a write on any edge, so they cannot back-pressure |

Every stall resolves when the manager asserts `bready` or `rready`. The block never waits on itself, so no deadlock is possible from the slave side.

## 11. Open points

- **OP-1.** Is a start only an EN transition from 0 to 1, or does a CTRL write with EN = 1 while running restart the count (TMR-START, TMR-RESTART-MODE)? This proposal keeps the running count, while still updating MODE and IE.
- **OP-2.** What is the COUNT value after a stop (TMR-STOP, TMR-STOP-EDGE, TMR-COUNT-READ)? This proposal holds the value.
- **OP-3.** For periodic mode with LOAD = 0 (TMR-LOAD-ZERO-PERIODIC), this proposal gives a count end on every edge after the start.
- **OP-4.** Is EXPIRED set on every periodic end (TMR-PERIODIC-EXPIRED-SET)? This proposal sets it on every end.
- **OP-5.** On a CTRL write on a count-end edge, this proposal suppresses the end so that CTRL wins (TMR-CTRL-WINS). The scope of that rule needs confirmation.
- **OP-6.** COUNT after a one-shot end is 0 in this proposal.
